newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam's son Uday gets up from his sick bed.
newsitem.headline: Saddam's son Uday gets up from his sick bed.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, shot and wounded in Baghdad two months ago, has appeared sitting in a wheelchair for the first time since the assassination attempt.

Uday was shown on his own Shebab television channel late on Tuesday night in a wheelchair, with his left leg still in bandages. During most of his appearances on television since the shooting Uday has been seen lying in his sick bed.

Tuesday's television footage showed him moving both hands at ease as he received senior officials on the Moslem feast of Eid al-Fitr. It was the first time that Uday, who was shot on December 10, was shown to be freely moving his left arm.
Press reports said earlier that Uday was on his way to full recovery despite claims by U.S. officials last month that he could lose one of his legs to gangrene.
Iraq blamed a pro-Iranian group for the attack on Uday and urged the United Nations last month to press Iran to hand over the attackers. Iranian officials have denied the charges.
Uday is chairman of Iraq's National Olympic Committee, owns Babel, Iraq's most popular newspaper, and runs the popular Shebab television channel.
